readings: (a) Budget exhaustion is treated like an unserved original: use the normalized canonical URL host as fallback, retain supported candidates and stop further calls.

(c) The hard budget stops calls, but unresolved-origin candidate handling needs a separate explicit assumption rather than either fallback being entailed.

Under R4-9, when the remaining budget cannot pay the whole plan, search and render returned pages first; start research only for an unsupported field with at least 3 units left after its 25-unit cost. Keep the latch at reservation time.
observe: Use remaining budget2 with a planned3-unit render or25-unit research before a1-unit search that can yield needed evidence; inspect whether the batch latches stopped or skips the expensive operation and continues cheaper work.
readings: (a) Once any next call cannot reserve its units, latch the entire batch stopped: no further provider call, even one cheap enough to fit; finish from evidence already obtained.
(b) Refuse only unaffordable calls but continue other planned affordable calls until no useful call fits, never exceeding the shared limit.
reading_requires: Never make a call that would exceed shared budget; finish remaining builds from gathered evidence, honoring contested/executive/investor semantics. The scope of stopping after one unaffordable call, despite cheaper remaining calls fitting, is unclear.

requires: Persist batches across restart and include every batch in native exports. For control exports, running builds follow R1-4 pre-build snapshots and count as not having run in batch spending; keep completed-build spending. Import resumes nothing and makes no provider call, imports batches done with owner visibility, and preserves the original POST replay body.
observe: Create completed and partially running native Stage4 batches, export, import unchanged into another process with no provider access, and inspect owner visibility, GET batch, dossier snapshots, original POST replay, costs and terminality; separately verify idle abrupt-restart equivalence.
readings: (a) Native exports preserve batch resources as service state too. Running builds are excluded/settled consistently with inherited pre-build export snapshots, import makes no provider call, and batch state/spending must be explicitly reconciled with those retained builds.

(b) Only restart persistence of batches is explicit; native export/import is required to preserve the earlier enumerated resources and completed idempotent responses but need not preserve GET batch resources.

(c) Native exports preserve running batch records and spending exactly while dossiers follow R1-4 pre-build snapshots; import then needs a specified no-provider terminalization rule to avoid stuck running batches.
reading_requires: Batches must survive restarts like other state. Whether inherited native export/import preservation also covers batch resources, and how an export taken during batch builds represents batch state/spending alongside R1-4 pre-build dossier snapshots, needs an explicit reading.
